AMZN.rationale: Amazon presents a solid fundamental case with strong trajectory, though tempered by meaningful near-term headwinds. On Pillar 1 (fundamentals & trajectory): The company shows accelerating revenue growth (Q3 2025: $180.2B, +7.4% QoQ; Q1 2026: $181.5B, +17% YoY per web context), with EPS rising from $1.59 to $1.95 across the three reported quarters. AWS is reaccelerating to 28% growth (fastest in 15 quarters), advertising is growing 22%+ YoY, and operating margins hit a record 13.1% in Q1 2026. The balance sheet is strong with $369.6B equity, $55.1B debt (0.149 debt-to-equity), and $101.8B+ cash. However, the massive ~$200B 2026 capex commitment has crushed free cash flow to just $1.2B TTM, and AWS profit concentration (~57-59% of operating income) creates dependency risk. On Pillar 2 (valuation): At a P/E of 32.2x, AMZN sits near the lower end of its 28.2-39.0x 12-month range, and P/B of 6.66x is at the bottom of its 5.8-8.3x range. This suggests fair-to-slightly-cheap valuation versus its own recent history, though not a screaming bargain. On Pillar 3 (near-term catalyst): Prime Day 2026 (June 23-26) is generating strong demand with $8.3B in first-day sales (+5.3% YoY), and Q2 earnings on July 30 could provide a positive catalyst if AWS momentum continues. However, these are partially offset by the FTC advertising complaint risk, EU DMA gatekeeper designation for AWS, and the October 2026 antitrust trial. The net catalyst picture is mixed rather than clearly positive.
